headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks exist; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an audio-speech agent with MCP/RAG tags, so it may ingest external content; Agent B is Argo Workflows with REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress, so A’s outputs could be routed into B-managed workflows. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertain, but the interaction is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF Agent A outputs are copied into an Argo workflow parameter or artifact path
IF Agent B parses A-produced text as instructions or templated commands
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from A to B; require manual review
Add provenance labels to A outputs before B consumes them
Restrict B templates to fixed schemas only
Use a quarantine step for any A-generated text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A reports no data classes touched and no network egress, while Agent B touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data class overlap, so leakage is not evidenced; the main risk is limited to accidental movement of artifacts through B if operators connect them.
conditions: IF operators place sensitive artifacts into a shared workspace consumed by B
IF A is later extended to emit files that B uploads through allowlisted egress
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in B artifacts or parameters
Review allowlisted destinations for B
Use redacted sample data for integration tests
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write surfaces and B exposes REST/GRPC APIs but no filesystem or git write capability is shown. Without overlapping mutable resources, direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not prove any shared write target.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API resource
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable artifact store
mitigations: Assign distinct resource namespaces
Avoid shared mutable API targets
Serialize writes through one controller
Document ownership of each artifact path
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can consume artifacts and parameters, so A’s outputs could become B’s inputs. Because B is a workflow engine, downstream actions may execute automatically if the pipeline trusts A without verification. The profiles do not show explicit validation, so the default risk is a plausible medium cascading error.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated artifacts or parameters without validation
IF the workflow triggers side effects after ingesting A output
mitigations: Insert a validation gate before B acts
Require human approval for A-derived inputs
Limit B to dry-run mode during integration
Log and diff A outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation and policy checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B only lists artifacts and parameters, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
IF retention or residency policies are introduced for shared data
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Avoid regulated data until policies are defined
Review deployment region settings
Add retention controls before production use
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
